entries.name: AI Town
entries.use_for: Deployable starter for a virtual town of AI characters
entries.why: MIT starter kit from a16z for agent simulations with a Convex backend; easy to customize.
entries.summary: Deployable starter kit for a virtual town where AI characters live, chat and socialize, inspired by the Generative Agents paper. Uses a Convex backend with shared global state, transactions and a simulation engine.
entries.best_for: Building agent-simulation or multiplayer AI-character experiments with a ready backend, from hobby projects to larger games.
entries.not_for: A starter and demo rather than a framework; tied to Convex for the backend and requires an LLM provider. Not suited for production agent orchestration use cases.

entries.name: Ant Design Pro
entries.use_for: Start an enterprise admin dashboard or back-office UI in React.
entries.why: Official Ant Design template with layouts, auth flows and dozens of ready pages for admin apps.
entries.summary: Official Ant Design React boilerplate for enterprise admin apps. Includes layouts, auth flows, TypeScript, block templates and many ready pages, built on Umi.
entries.best_for: Starting an enterprise back-office or admin dashboard in React with Ant Design components.
entries.not_for: Locked to the Ant Design/Umi ecosystem and its visual style. Heavy for small projects, and it is frontend-only with no backend included.

entries.name: ASP.NET Boilerplate
entries.use_for: Starting point for ASP.NET Core apps with DDD, multi-tenancy and auth
entries.why: Mature .NET application template and framework behind ABP; MIT.
entries.summary: General purpose application framework and template for ASP.NET Core, with DDD layering, multi-tenancy, authorization and modular design. Underlies ASP.NET Zero.
entries.best_for: Maintaining existing ABP-based .NET apps that already depend on it.
entries.not_for: Support officially ends May 2026; the README recommends migrating to ABP Framework for new projects. .NET only.

entries.name: Bulletproof React
entries.use_for: Opinionated, scalable React application architecture with sample apps
entries.why: Widely referenced React architecture with example apps for Vite, Next.js and React Router
entries.summary: Opinionated architecture guide for scalable React apps, with a project structure, practices and sample applications for Vite, Next.js (app and pages) and React Router.
entries.best_for: Learning or copying a feature-based React folder structure and conventions for a growing production app.
entries.not_for: A reference/example repo, not an installable library or CLI scaffold. Opinions (library choices, structure) may not fit every team.

entries.name: Chrome Extension TypeScript Starter
entries.use_for: Start a Chrome extension written in TypeScript.
entries.why: Minimal, well-known starter with build setup for background, content and popup scripts.
entries.summary: Minimal starter for a Chrome extension written in TypeScript, with an npm build and watch setup. Includes an options page, a content script, a badge counter and a background script.
entries.best_for: Quickly bootstrapping a simple TypeScript Chrome extension with no framework.
entries.not_for: Bare-bones: no UI framework or bundler extras, and the manifest version may be dated; check before use. Chrome-focused only.

entries.name: Cookiecutter Data Science
entries.use_for: Standard project structure for data science work
entries.why: Widely adopted, opinionated layout for reproducible data science projects
entries.summary: Python tool that generates a standardized, flexible project structure for data science work, installed as the cookiecutter-data-science package. v2 differs from v1 and extends cookiecutter functionality.
entries.best_for: Starting reproducible data science or ML projects with a consistent layout for data, notebooks and code.
entries.not_for: Only a scaffold with a folder convention; it provides no pipeline, experiment tracking or deployment tooling. Opinionated structure may not suit all teams.

entries.name: Cookiecutter Django
entries.use_for: Generate a production-ready Django project with Docker, auth and settings done right.
entries.why: The standard Django starting point, generating a secure 12-factor setup with Celery and deployment options.
entries.summary: Cookiecutter template that generates a production-ready Django project with Docker, 12-factor settings, authentication and Celery, plus multiple deployment options.
entries.best_for: Starting a new Django project with sensible, secure defaults and Docker deployment already configured.
entries.not_for: Python/Django only and fairly opinionated; generates many files and configs you may need to strip for small prototypes.

entries.name: Electron React Boilerplate
entries.use_for: Start a cross-platform Electron desktop app with React and TypeScript.
entries.why: Long-standing Electron + React template with packaging, hot reload and auto-update preconfigured.
entries.summary: Electron plus React and TypeScript template with hot reload, packaging for production and auto-update support preconfigured.
entries.best_for: Starting a cross-platform desktop app using Electron with React.
entries.not_for: Electron's large footprint; README is sparse and defers to external docs. Not for mobile or web-only apps, and React/webpack choices are fixed.

entries.name: Full Stack FastAPI Template
entries.use_for: Full-stack template: FastAPI, SQLModel, Postgres, React, Docker Compose and CI
entries.why: Official FastAPI template with auth, tests and deploy setup out of the box
entries.summary: Official full-stack template with a FastAPI backend, SQLModel and PostgreSQL, a React frontend (TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind, shadcn/ui) with an auto-generated client, Docker Compose and CI.
entries.best_for: Starting a Python API plus React web app with auth, tests and deploy setup already wired up.
entries.not_for: Opinionated stack (FastAPI, Postgres, React); heavy for tiny projects or non-React frontends. Not a multi-tenant SaaS kit.

entries.name: go-admin
entries.use_for: Gin + Vue admin starter with RBAC and code generation
entries.why: Popular Go admin scaffold with permissions, menus and code generator; MIT.
entries.summary: Admin system scaffold with a Go (Gin) backend and Vue frontend (Element UI, Arco Design or Ant Design). Provides RESTful APIs, permission management, menus and a code generator, initialized by editing database configuration.
entries.best_for: Building Go-based back-office apps with role-based access and quick CRUD code generation.
entries.not_for: Go/Gin and Vue only; documentation is largely geared to Chinese-speaking users. Heavy if you only need an API.

entries.name: Hackathon Starter
entries.use_for: Node.js/Express boilerplate with auth and API integrations
entries.why: Ready OAuth logins, account management and many API examples; ideal for fast prototypes.
entries.summary: Node.js and Express boilerplate with ready-made OAuth sign-ins, account management and many API integration examples, aimed at quickly starting prototypes.
entries.best_for: Hackathons and quick prototypes needing social login and sample API integrations.
entries.not_for: Server-rendered Express app with many unused example features; not a modern production architecture and needs stripping down for serious projects.

entries.name: HTML5 Boilerplate
entries.use_for: Front-end template for fast, robust static websites
entries.why: Long-standing baseline template for web projects (57k stars), maintained by H5BP.
entries.summary: Long-running front-end template for fast, robust static sites and web apps. Provides sensible defaults and configuration without imposing a framework or development philosophy.
entries.best_for: Starting plain HTML/CSS/JS sites with good baseline defaults and no framework.
entries.not_for: Not a component framework or build system; modern framework starters (Vite, Next.js) cover app development better.

entries.name: Hugoplate
entries.use_for: Start a static marketing site or blog with Hugo and Tailwind CSS.
entries.why: Actively maintained Hugo + Tailwind v4 starter with blog, SEO and multilingual support.
entries.summary: Hugo and Tailwind CSS v4 starter for blogs and marketing sites. Includes multi-authors, search, dark mode, tags and categories, similar posts, contact form, multilingual support and Netlify config.
entries.best_for: Static marketing sites or blogs built with Hugo that need SEO and multilingual features out of the box.
entries.not_for: Hugo/Tailwind static site only; no dynamic backend or app features. Customizing means working within the template's structure.

entries.name: Ignite
entries.use_for: React Native/Expo boilerplate with CLI and generators
entries.why: Infinite Red's battle-tested RN starter used for years in production apps.

license_verified.note: LICENSE file is MIT, read from raw.githubusercontent.com

entries.summary: React Native boilerplate with a CLI and generators, maintained since 2016. Sets up an Expo-based app with a recommended structure and tooling.
entries.best_for: Starting a React Native/Expo app with an opinionated structure and code generators.
entries.not_for: Opinionated stack choices (including state and navigation) may not match yours; mobile React Native only.

entries.name: JHipster
entries.use_for: Generate Spring Boot + Angular/React/Vue apps and microservices
entries.why: Widely used generator for full-stack Java apps with auth, CI and deploy configs; Apache-2.0.
entries.summary: Yeoman-based generator that scaffolds Spring Boot backends with Angular, React or Vue frontends, and microservices, including auth, CI and deployment configuration.
entries.best_for: Java teams wanting a generated full-stack app or microservices architecture with conventions already set.
entries.not_for: Heavy and opinionated Java/Spring stack with a learning curve; generated code is large and hard to diverge from. Not for lightweight projects.

entries.name: n8n Self-hosted AI Starter Kit
entries.use_for: Spin up a local AI workflow stack (n8n, Ollama, Qdrant, Postgres) with Docker Compose.
entries.why: Official n8n template bundling a local LLM, vector store and workflow engine in one compose file.
entries.summary: Docker Compose template that bundles self-hosted n8n with Ollama (local LLMs), Qdrant (vector store) and Postgres for building local AI workflows with low-code tooling.
entries.best_for: Quickly spinning up a private local AI workflow environment with RAG-style components.
entries.not_for: A starter for local experimentation, not a hardened production deployment. Local models need adequate GPU/CPU resources, and n8n has its own license terms.

entries.name: NestJS Boilerplate
entries.use_for: Start a NestJS REST API with auth, database, mailing, i18n and Docker in place.
entries.why: Well-maintained NestJS starter supporting TypeORM/Postgres or Mongoose, with social login and tests.
entries.summary: NestJS REST API boilerplate with TypeORM or Mongoose, seeding, email/social auth (Apple, Facebook, Google), roles, i18n, file uploads (local or S3), mailing, Swagger, tests, Docker and CI.
entries.best_for: Starting a NestJS backend with auth, database, mailing and file uploads already in place.
entries.not_for: NestJS/TypeScript only; includes many features you may need to strip. Backend only, with no frontend.

entries.name: Next Shadcn Dashboard Starter
entries.use_for: Admin dashboard starter with Next.js App Router, shadcn/ui, auth, tables and charts
entries.why: Popular Next.js admin starter with data tables, forms and kanban ready to extend
entries.summary: Free MIT admin dashboard starter with Next.js 16, shadcn/ui, Tailwind v4 and TypeScript. Includes working data tables, forms, auth, organizations and billing, with a cleanup script to remove unneeded parts.
entries.best_for: Starting an admin panel or SaaS dashboard on Next.js with real functional tables and forms.
entries.not_for: Next.js and shadcn only; not a full SaaS backend by itself, and some features may rely on third-party services such as Clerk.

entries.name: next-forge
entries.use_for: Start a production Next.js SaaS monorepo with auth, billing, analytics and docs.
entries.why: Vercel-maintained Turborepo template that wires best-in-class services together in a clean monorepo.
entries.summary: Turborepo template for production Next.js SaaS apps. An opinionated monorepo that integrates auth, billing, analytics, docs and other services with minimal configuration.
entries.best_for: Launching a SaaS on Next.js that needs a full monorepo with integrated third-party services.
entries.not_for: Heavy and opinionated; many bundled services and packages are overkill for small apps. Tied to Next.js and its chosen vendors.

entries.name: Next.js Boilerplate
entries.use_for: Start a Next.js app with Tailwind, TypeScript, auth, DB, testing and linting preconfigured.
entries.why: Popular, frequently updated boilerplate with strong DX defaults (Drizzle, Vitest, Playwright, Storybook).
entries.summary: Next.js 16 App Router boilerplate with Tailwind v4 and TypeScript, plus Clerk auth, DrizzleORM (Postgres, SQLite, MySQL), Vitest, Playwright, Storybook, Sentry, i18n and linting tooling.
entries.best_for: Starting a Next.js app with strong developer-experience defaults for testing and linting.
entries.not_for: Opinionated stack tied to specific vendors (Clerk, Sentry, etc.); lots of tooling to remove for small projects. Not a SaaS kit with billing.

entries.name: Next.js Enterprise Boilerplate
entries.use_for: Enterprise-grade Next.js boilerplate with testing, CI, Storybook and observability
entries.why: Well-maintained production setup for larger Next.js teams
entries.summary: Production-oriented Next.js boilerplate for larger teams, with testing, CI, Storybook, observability and infrastructure provisioning options such as AWS (ECS, VPC, CloudFront).
entries.best_for: Enterprise or larger-team Next.js projects needing CI, testing, observability and cloud infrastructure scaffolding.
entries.not_for: Too heavy for small or solo projects; opinionated infra setup (e.g. AWS) you may need to adapt or remove.

entries.name: Obytes React Native Template
entries.use_for: Start an Expo React Native app with TypeScript, styling, forms and testing set up.
entries.why: Opinionated, actively maintained Expo template with NativeWind, React Query, i18n and CI.
entries.summary: Expo React Native template with TypeScript, TailwindCSS (NativeWind), expo-router, React Query, TanStack Form, i18n, Husky and lint-staged.
entries.best_for: Starting a production-minded Expo app with a modern, opinionated stack.
entries.not_for: Opinionated library choices; mobile React Native only. May lag Expo upgrades if you need the newest SDK.

entries.name: Open SaaS
entries.use_for: Start a full SaaS app with auth, payments, admin dashboard and AI examples already wired up.
entries.why: Free, full-featured SaaS boilerplate on Wasp (React + Node + Prisma) with Stripe/Polar, email and docs.
entries.summary: Free SaaS starter built on Wasp (React, Node.js, Prisma). Includes auth, payments (Stripe/Polar), email, admin dashboard, AI examples and docs, and is set up to work with AI coding tools.
entries.best_for: Launching a full SaaS quickly with auth, payments and an admin dashboard already wired.
entries.not_for: Requires adopting the Wasp framework, which is less common than plain Next.js. Stack is fixed to React, Node and Prisma.

entries.name: React Starter Kit
entries.use_for: React + Bun + tRPC + Tailwind starter deployable to Cloudflare Workers
entries.why: Modern, maintained full-stack React template with Stripe and edge deployment.
entries.summary: Full-stack monorepo template for SaaS with React 19, tRPC, Drizzle ORM and Neon Postgres, deployed as three Cloudflare Workers. Includes Better Auth (OTP, passkeys, Google OAuth, organizations) and Stripe subscriptions.
entries.best_for: Edge-deployed, end-to-end type-safe SaaS on Cloudflare.
entries.not_for: Targets Cloudflare Workers and Bun specifically; not for traditional Node hosting or other frontend frameworks.

entries.name: SaaS Boilerplate
entries.use_for: Next.js SaaS boilerplate with auth, multi-tenancy, roles, i18n, billing and tests
entries.why: Feature-complete multi-tenant SaaS starter with Drizzle, shadcn/ui and full testing setup
entries.summary: Next.js and Tailwind SaaS template with shadcn/ui. Provides authentication, multi-tenancy with teams, roles and permissions, Drizzle DB, i18n, landing page, dashboard, Sentry, tests and user impersonation.
entries.best_for: Building a multi-tenant SaaS on Next.js that needs teams, roles and billing basics.
entries.not_for: Next.js and its chosen services only; sizeable codebase to learn. Some features rely on third-party vendors such as Clerk.

entries.name: Shadcn Admin
entries.use_for: Admin dashboard template built with shadcn/ui, Vite and TanStack Router
entries.why: Popular polished admin UI starter with many ready pages
entries.summary: Admin dashboard UI built with shadcn/ui, Vite and TanStack Router. Features light/dark mode, responsive and accessible design, sidebar, global search command, 10+ pages and RTL support.
entries.best_for: Reusing a polished dashboard UI for an admin panel in a Vite React app.
entries.not_for: The README says it is not a starter template; it is a UI collection without backend, data layer or auth logic of its own.

entries.name: Vercel Chatbot
entries.use_for: Full-featured AI chatbot template with Next.js and the AI SDK
entries.why: Vercel's reference chat app template: streaming, persistence, auth and artifacts
entries.summary: Vercel's reference chatbot template built with Next.js App Router and the AI SDK. Supports multiple model providers via the AI Gateway, streaming, chat persistence, auth and artifacts.
entries.best_for: Starting an AI chat app with streaming, history and auth on Next.js.
entries.not_for: Tied to Next.js, Vercel's AI SDK and a database/auth setup; heavier than needed for a simple chat widget.

entries.name: Your Next Store
entries.use_for: Start a fast Next.js storefront backed by Stripe products and checkout.
entries.why: Lean open-source commerce starter using Stripe as the product catalog, avoiding a separate commerce backend.
entries.summary: Open-source Next.js e-commerce template that uses Stripe as the product catalog and for checkout, billing and subscriptions. Ships AGENTS.md and a typed Commerce Kit SDK for AI coding tools.
entries.best_for: Small to medium storefronts where Stripe products are the catalog and you want no separate commerce backend.
entries.not_for: Stripe-only and Next.js-only; lacks the inventory, multi-warehouse and admin depth of full commerce platforms.
